title: Advanced Grammar
description: Master complex grammatical structures to improve your writing.
competenceGoals: use key patterns for sentences, verb forms, and text construction in communication

content.content:
# Advanced Grammar Structures

In 9th grade, you will learn more complex grammar that helps you express nuanced ideas.
This includes:
- Conditionals (if-sentences)
- Passive voice
- Reported speech
- Relative clauses

content.title: Conditionals
content.content:
**Zero conditional:** General truths
- If + present, present
- "If you heat water to 100°C, it boils."

**First conditional:** Real possibilities (future)
- If + present, will + verb
- "If it rains tomorrow, we will stay inside."

**Second conditional:** Unreal/hypothetical (present/future)
- If + past, would + verb
- "If I won the lottery, I would travel the world."

**Third conditional:** Unreal past
- If + past perfect, would have + past participle
- "If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam."

content.title: Using Conditionals
content.solution:
**Zero:** If you _____ (mix) yellow and blue, you get green.
**Answer:** If you **mix** yellow and blue, you get green.

**First:** If she _____ (study), she will pass.
**Answer:** If she **studies**, she will pass.

**Second:** If I _____ (be) taller, I would play basketball.
**Answer:** If I **were** taller, I would play basketball.
(Note: "were" is used for all persons in the second conditional)

**Third:** If they _____ (leave) earlier, they wouldn't have missed the bus.
**Answer:** If they **had left** earlier, they wouldn't have missed the bus.

content.title: Passive Voice
content.content:
**Active:** The subject performs the action
- "Shakespeare wrote Hamlet."

**Passive:** The subject receives the action
- "Hamlet was written by Shakespeare."

**Form:** be + past participle (+ by + agent)

**When to use passive:**
- When the action is more important than who did it
- When we don't know who did it
- In formal or scientific writing

**Examples:**
- Active: Someone stole my bike.
- Passive: My bike was stolen. (we don't know who)

content.title: Reported Speech
content.content:
When reporting what someone said, we usually shift the tense back:

**Present → Past:**
- Direct: "I am tired," she said.
- Reported: She said (that) she was tired.

**Past → Past Perfect:**
- Direct: "I saw him," he said.
- Reported: He said (that) he had seen him.

**Will → Would:**
- Direct: "I will help," she said.
- Reported: She said (that) she would help.

**Other changes:**
- "this" → "that"
- "here" → "there"
- "today" → "that day"

exercise.solution: Choosing the right conditional depends on how real or hypothetical the situation is.

exercise.task: Change these sentences to passive voice:

subTasks.label: b
subTasks.solution: Dinner is being prepared (by the chef).

subTasks.label: c
subTasks.task: They will announce the winner tomorrow.
subTasks.solution: The winner will be announced tomorrow.

exercise.solution: Passive voice emphasizes the action rather than who performs it.

subTasks.label: a
subTasks.task: "I am going to the cinema," he said.
subTasks.solution: He said (that) he was going to the cinema.

subTasks.label: b
subTasks.solution: She promised (that) they would meet the next day.

subTasks.label: c
subTasks.task: "I have never been to Paris," he admitted.
subTasks.solution: He admitted (that) he had never been to Paris.
